title: Three-point claim kicker notebook
content:
Purpose:
Quick, portable scratchpad to crystallize three priority claims I want to land in my midquarter check-in with my manager. Keep it short, defensible, and runnable as a 10-minute conversation.

How to use this doc:
- Top: the three claims (one line each)
- Middle: 2–4 bullets of evidence per claim (metrics, dates, outcomes, names)
- Bottom: ask(s) — specific, time-boxed, and binary where possible
- At end: potential pushback + one-liner responses

Date of next sync: 2026-02-16 (30 min)
Timebox goal: 8–10 minutes of claims + 5 minutes alignment on asks

---
Top 3 claim headlines (elevator):
1) I led a cross-functional pilot that cut inference e2e latency by 18% for the payment-qa endpoint, improving user test throughput and slashing timeout incidents.
2) I created the new onboarding checklist + mentor pairing for new POs that reduced time-to-first-contribution from 5 weeks to ~2.5 weeks across the last cohort.
3) I owned the Q1 operational runbook updates and implemented two incident playbooks that decreased MTTD for infra-related regressions from 42m to 17m.

Scratch evidence (brief, timestamped):
Claim 1 (latency reduction):
- Jan 4–Jan 26 pilot with serving-runtime and infra: rolled out KV-cache warmup + request prioritization on canary machines.
- Quant: p50 latency from 240ms -> 198ms; p95 from 1.1s -> 0.9s (calibration windows: 2pm–4pm PST traffic slice).
- Incidents: timeouts for payment-qa reduced from 9 -> 2 in the month following rollout (JIRA-HR-4567 refs).
- Signal: internal benchmark dashboard snapshot (contrib: Jonah Lee for telemetry; PR: github.com/redwood/infra#1458).
- Notes: slight increase in tail CPU on canary (observed 4%); scheduled follow-up with infra team to validate autoscaling threshold.

Claim 2 (onboarding):
- Created checklist doc (link: CONFLUENCE-OPS-1123) and enacted pairing program starting cohort Jan 12.
- New hire metrics: first meaningful PR (% of new hires with merged PR) improved cohort-over-cohort from 28% -> 64% within first 3 weeks.
- Mentor feedback: qualitative notes — mentors report less onboarding noise; ref Slack thread (people-ops thread #8321).
- Cost: 2 hrs/week mentor time allocation per new hire; tradeoff justified by faster ramp.

Claim 3 (incident playbooks):
- Updated runbook v2 (Feb 2) with decision trees and communication templates.
- War room drills: ran two drills in Jan -> median MTTD dropped 42m -> 17m in Feb for similar severity incidents.
- Postmortems: two follow-ups (incident-2026-01-19 & incident-2026-01-28) marked as resolved with action owners assigned.
- Cross-team: engaged SRE (Anika), infra (Jonah), and serving-runtime (Ravi) to validate steps.

Concrete asks (what I want from manager in this meeting):
- Primary ask: Sign-off to convert the latency pilot into a dedicated 3-week project with 0.4 FTE infra + 0.6 FTE serving-runtime allocation (goal: ship autoscaling threshold tweak and KV-warmup library). Target start: Feb 23.
- Secondary ask: Sponsor approval to formalize mentor pairing as 0.5 FTE overhead for Q2 hiring batch (budget ask: estimate attached in Confluence).
- Tertiary ask: Advocate for an ops-oncall rotation pilot (1 month) to test if runbook familiarity reduces MTTI for low-sev alerts. Need manager to back scheduling and partner with SRE lead.

Success criteria for asks (how we'll measure):
- Latency project: defined OKR (p95 reduction >= 10% on payment-qa during 2–6pm PST synthetic traffic), merged PRs tagged, and a short readout in 6 weeks.
- Mentor program: time-to-first-merged-PR <= 3 weeks for next cohort; mentor feedback survey average >= 4/5.
- Oncall pilot: record MTTD/MITT for pilot period and compare against prior 12-week baseline.

Potential pushback and my one-liner responses:
- "We don't have headcount / bandwidth." -> "I propose a 3-week focused pilot that uses 0.6 FTE from serving-runtime and a one-time mentoring stipend; if outcomes aren't clear in 6 weeks we stop."
- "Mentoring adds overhead to ICs." -> "We already see productivity gains; the small upfront time investment returns via faster ramp and fewer hand-holding tickets."
- "Ops-oncall increases wake-up risk." -> "Pilot design has strict severity bounds; it's workload-limited and paired with runbook automation to reduce pager noise."

Open questions / follow-ups before sync:
- Confirm with Jonah whether additional telemetry instrumentation needs infra approval or is covered by existing ticket (follow up: ping Jonah in Slack).
- Draft brief one-pager for manager (1-page PDF) summarizing pilot budget and timeline — aim to circulate Feb 14.
- Get mentor hourly commitment confirmed by Feb 10 so I can budget for Q2 cohort.

Quick meeting script (10 min):
0:00–0:45 min — one-sentence context + three claims (30–45s each)
0:45–4:00 min — show 1 slide / one data snippet per claim (focus on metric change + tradeoffs)
4:00–7:00 min — asks + success criteria (be explicit on what I need)
7:00–9:00 min — manager feedback, blockers, next steps, who signs off
9:00–10:00 min — confirm owners, calendar tasks, and communication plan

To-dos after meeting (my checklist):
- Create project brief + assign ticket to infra and serving-runtime (due Feb 20).
- Update Confluence with final ask and budget numbers.
- Share mentor pairing schedule and mentor roster.
- Set up 3-week cadence check-ins and assign measurable tracking for OKRs.

Quick private notes / tone cues:
- Keep it concrete, metric-first. Avoid long narratives.
- Show that I've done a small-scale test already (reduces risk).
- Make asks binary: yes/no for pilot, not vague resource asks.
- If manager asks for more time, suggest a 48-hour turnaround for the one-pager.

Random scratch space (brain dump):
- Consider adding a short win: "reduced developer queue time" metric — need to pull from JIRA to quantify.
- Maybe offer to trade mentoring stipend for one less headcount in Q2? rough thought.
- If we get green light, schedule kickoff Feb 23 and invite SRE + infra leads.

End of doc.

(Version note: this is a live scratchpad. Intended to be pared down into a 1-page manager brief after alignment.)
